## Summary

In October 2025, Sanae Takaichi was elected on October 21st as Japan's first female Prime Minister. She won 237 votes in the lower house and replaced Shigeru Ishiba, who had been prime minister for just over a year. Takaichi had been appointed president of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on October 4th following Ishiba's resignation, and now leads a minority government formed as part of a coalition with the Japan Innovation Party.

## Summary of Search Results

Japan's Diet (parliament) nominated Sanae Takaichi, president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, as the new prime minister to succeed Shigeru Ishiba on October 21, 2025. Takaichi became Japan's 104th Prime Minister, marking a historic milestone as she is the first woman to hold the office.

Takaichi secured 237 votes, defeating Yoshihiko Noda of the Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan, who received 149 votes. She launched her cabinet Tuesday evening after the attestation ceremonies for the new prime minister and other cabinet members. The LDP is slated to form a coalition government with Nippon Ishin no Kai (Japan Innovation Party) after Komeito ended its ruling coalition with the LDP earlier that month.
